research_updates.title: Original incentive audit findings remain campus-level
research_updates.notes: GOED's fiscal-year 2012 audit table reports 83 jobs, a $38.42 average wage, and $689,829,656 of capital expenditure for Apple after compliant two- and five-year audits. The table does not allocate the findings among buildings, separate construction from equipment, or report realized tax receipts or public-service costs.

source.title: Approved Tax Abatement Biennial Report, Fiscal Years 2010 through 2022
source.publisher: Nevada Governor's Office of Economic Development
source.notes: The fiscal-year 2012 two-year and five-year audit table places Apple's June 30, 2012 effective contract in Washoe County. It reports original projections of 35 jobs, a $25.00 average wage, and $400 million capital expenditure, then reports audit findings of 83 jobs, a $38.42 average wage, and $689,829,656 capital expenditure. The table marks both the June 30, 2014 two-year audit and June 30, 2017 five-year audit compliant. The reported capital total is broad and is not treated as construction-only spending, a tax receipt, or an amount attributable to one campus building.

research_updates.title: Expansion packet preserves forecasts rather than realized effects
research_updates.notes: GOED packet query Apple Inc./21505 Reno Technology Parkway W reviewed all 16 pages. It separately schedules $163 million of construction, $742,071,428 of first-five-year equipment, ten additional FTE at $32.51, $200,909,110 of projected local taxes, and $62,153,275 of estimated abatement. No board-order, tax-return, invoice, payroll, or later audit in the packet converts those forecasts into actuals.

source.title: Apple expansion application — Nevada GOED board packet, July 25, 2024
source.publisher: Nevada Governor’s Office of Economic Development
source.notes: Existing workforce is company-reported in the application signed June 13, 2024. Detailed schedules are redacted in the public packet.

research_updates.title: Exact-address permit search adds direct construction observations without summing scopes
research_updates.notes: Searched Washoe County permit-report family for 2012-2026 using 21505 RENO TECHNOLOGY PKWY W, APPLE INC, PROJECT HUCKLEBERRY and PROJECT ISABEL. Main records located: 15-3589 ($37,913,134.77), 16-2026 ($9,140,880), and WBLD17-100303 ($50,720,905.86). Also located 15-3956, 16-1555, WBLD17-100612, WBLD17-102177 and WBLD17-103570 through -103582; those subordinate or zero-value permits are not added to the main permits because overlap cannot be excluded.

source.title: Washoe County Permit Activity Report, permits issued July 1 through December 31, 2017
source.notes: Exact-address search located Huckleberry Phase 2 permit 16-2026, Isabel permit WBLD17-100303, a $400,000 septic-system permit, a $1,261,320 fire-sprinkler permit, and named contractors. Only distinct main construction permits are normalized; subpermits are not added to them.

research_updates.title: Assessor, treasurer and recorder review yields parcel stocks but no receipt series
research_updates.notes: Searched Washoe Assessor secured rolls for Apple and APNs 084-110-20, 084-110-29, 084-110-30, 084-110-36, 084-110-37, 084-191-05 through -08 for tax years 2021/22 and 2024/25; normalized only main-campus APN 084-110-29. Queried the Treasurer parcel/owner portal and Recorder APN guidance. Public indexed results did not verify taxes paid, recipient-level receipts, delinquency/payment dates, or a complete deed consideration series; assessed values are therefore not converted to fiscal revenue.

source.title: Washoe County 2024/2025 Secured Assessment Roll
source.notes: The later owner-indexed roll supplies a comparable APN 084-110-29 assessed land and building stock. The roll expressly says the Assessor values property but does not set rates or collect taxes.

research_updates.title: Planning cases separate campus buildout, substations and fire-station parcel
research_updates.notes: Reviewed Washoe planning families SW11-001/SW11-003, WSUP17-0008, WSUP18-0010, WAC23-0012, WSUP23-0031 and WTPM24-0007. Records map APNs and describe substation/building phases and a parcel for a fire station, but do not report realized Apple construction spend, facility load, fire-service operating cost, tax receipts, or building allocation. The fire-station parcel is not treated as a data-center building or quantified public cost.

source.title: Tentative Parcel Map WTPM24-0007 staff report, Parcel Map for Apple Incorporated
source.notes: The application identifies Apple as owner of APN 084-191-08, 180.92 acres at the campus address, and proposes a separate parcel for a fire station. It is retained to prevent the fire-station parcel from being collapsed into the data-center building account.

research_updates.title: GOED amendment, compliance and audit follow-up finds no realized 2024 expansion amount
research_updates.notes: Searched GOED board packets, notices/minutes and NRS 231.0685 biennial reports through FY2024 for Apple, Washoe, data center, amendment, audit and compliance. The 2025 biennial report repeats the June 2012 account's 2017 audit findings. It does not show a completed audit, realized abatement, realized tax payment, or amended audited employment/capital result for the July 2024 expansion application.

source.title: GOED Biennial Report to Legislature of Abatements from Taxation, fiscal years 2010 through 2024
source.publisher: Nevada Governor's Office of Economic Development
source.notes: The newer report repeats the original Apple FY2012 audit result and separately lists FY2024 program material. It does not add a completed audit or realized company-specific tax amount for Apple's July 2024 expansion packet.

research_updates.title: Nevada Tax Commission and Department of Taxation searches remain aggregate
research_updates.notes: Searched 2015-2026 Nevada Department of Taxation tax-expenditure reports, ad-valorem projections, Commission meeting archive and State Board of Equalization material for Apple, 084-110-29, Washoe, data center and abatement. Results were program- or jurisdiction-level; no Apple-specific realized sales/use abatement, property-tax payment, local receipt, appeal outcome, or 2024 expansion audit was verified.

source.title: Nevada Department of Taxation tax-expenditure reports and public meeting archive
source.notes: Entity-name, APN, county, data-center and abatement searches across published 2015-2026 report and meeting families produced aggregate tax-expenditure and jurisdiction projections but no Apple-specific realized receipt, payment, or 2024 expansion audit.

research_updates.title: PUCN and NV Energy dockets triangulate renewable assets but not campus bills
research_updates.notes: Searched PUCN electric/renewable docket families and rate pages for Apple and dockets 12-11023, 13-07005, 15-11025, 17-02008 and 17-11002. Official filings confirm GreenEnergy Rider agreements, capacities, commissioning and 2022 project generation/REC transfers. They do not disclose Apple's campus kWh, demand, bill, tariff charge, avoided cost, or hourly resource matching; the independent campus-use observation comes from Apple instead.

source.title: NV Energy Portfolio Standard Annual Report, Compliance Year 2022
source.publisher: NV Energy filing with the Public Utilities Commission of Nevada
source.notes: The filing reports 560,408 MWh from 200 MW Techren Solar 2 and 112,268 MWh from 50 MW Turquoise Nevada Solar in 2022, with equal renewable-energy credits transferred to Apple. Those project outputs are not relabeled as facility consumption.

research_updates.title: Water and sewer review finds a private system and capacity, not measured use
research_updates.notes: Searched TMWA board reports/current data-center guidance, Washoe water-right agenda items, Northern Nevada Public Health public-water-system references, and planning/permit text for Reno Technology Park, Apple, water, sewer, septic and wastewater from 2012-2026. County material identifies 125 acre-feet/year allocated to the data center; TMWA calls the system private. No meter, actual withdrawal/consumption, peak-day value, wastewater discharge, utility bill, or current same-scope sewer-cost series was found.

source.title: TMWA staff report on private, cooperative and general-improvement-district water systems
source.notes: TMWA identifies the Reno Technology Park (Apple Data Center) water system as a private system outside TMWA's retail system. The report supplies no Apple meter, withdrawal, consumption, discharge, or bill.

research_updates.title: Apple facilities archive supplies a 2025 campus electricity observation
research_updates.notes: Reviewed Apple Facilities Report 2013, Environmental Progress Reports 2023-2026, environment report archive, job-creation and newsroom pages for Reno/Nevada/data center. The 2026 report gives 422 million kWh in 2025 and cooling/renewable context. No Reno water volume, wastewater, power cost, building split, construction invoice, supplier payment, or public-service cost appears in the reviewed operator family.

source.title: Apple Environmental Progress Report 2026
source.notes: Apple reports fiscal-2025 Mesa electricity use, the supporting Bonnybrooke project's capacity, onsite PV capacity and operating dates. Electricity is operator-reported use; generating capacities are nameplate resources and not data-center load or output observations.

research_updates.title: Workforce and job-posting search identifies occupations but not realized headcount
research_updates.notes: Queried Apple Careers for Sparks/Reno/Nevada/data center and reviewed role IDs 200653833-6172, 200653810-6172, 200653832-6172, 200673896-6172 and 200674135-6172 plus data-center operations role 200665517-6172. These current postings document recruiting and occupation mix, but not filled positions, vacancies net of churn, worker residence, annual-average FTE, wages paid, benefits, payroll, or contractor headcount.

source.title: Apple Careers search results for Sparks, Nevada
source.notes: The current search showed data-center construction project manager, mechanical project manager, controls engineer, and data-center operations roles in Sparks. Posting counts and roles are recruiting signals, not filled jobs, annual-average FTE, residence, payroll, or wage observations.

research_updates.title: Procurement and vendor search verifies roles but no payment amounts
research_updates.notes: Permit records name FCI Group, Simplex Grinnell, Desert Fire Protection, Stantec and project applicants on Apple-address work; Apple newsroom material separately describes K&N filter prototyping and a Nevada sheet-metal fabricator. Searches for Apple Reno vendor, contractor, procurement, purchase order and supplier payment found no contract value attributable to a named vendor, local-retained share, vendor payroll, or worker residence. Permit value remains construction evidence rather than supplier revenue.

source.title: Washoe County Permit Activity Report, permits issued May 1 through August 31, 2018
source.notes: The later report verifies final status for WBLD17-100303 and lists multiple $140,000 cluster fire-alarm permits. The alarm permits are not summed with the main permit because they may be embedded in the broader shell/buildout scope.

research_updates.title: Named-recipient review verifies bounded gifts but not campus attribution
research_updates.notes: Searched official Envirolution, Children's Cabinet and Food Bank of Northern Nevada reports for Apple, grant, donation and Reno across 2020-2026. Food Bank recipient reports place Apple in the $10,000-$24,999 band in both 2021-2022 and 2022-2023; $10,000 lower bounds are recorded separately. Envirolution reports program activity near an Apple data center but not a clearly Apple-funded amount. No exact campus-designated annual community total was found.

source.title: Food Bank of Northern Nevada 2022-2023 Annual Report
source.notes: Recipient report again places Apple Inc. in the $10,000-$24,999 donor band. The lower bound is normalized without treating it as recurring campus spending.

economic_scope_note: Reviewed evidence batches at campus or company/county scope. No record is allocated to an individual inventory building. Source checking establishes what a document reports, not an independent audit or causal attribution. Monetary figures are nominal. Peak workforce is distinct from annual employment; source-year labels do not establish fiscal-year boundaries. Original forecasts remain forecasts until realization is verified. No cross-record benefit total is defined. Cumulative project costs are not annual expenditure. Tax receipts and incentive payments remain separate, with inferred taxpayer links disclosed. Contextual research updates do not count as economic amounts. Account tax bills are distinct from cash receipts and incentive-program fees. Tax years, calendar years and fiscal years retain their source basis; separate taxpayer accounts are not consolidated. Municipal developer rebates and taxpayer valuations have distinct subjects. Estimated actual property value and tax capacity are not tax receipts; payable-year valuations retain their earlier assessment date. Taxpayer values expressed in millions retain approximate precision and account-level separation. A current-year table can use an older valuation date and is not converted into an annual series. Facility real-property and business-personal-property accounts remain separate, and address-label discrepancies are disclosed. Michigan Industrial Facilities Tax accounts remain distinct from the underlying real parcel and from post-expiration personal-property accounts; annual account totals are not recipient-level government receipts. Permit construction values are administrative project amounts, not verified expenditure, and separate permits are not combined without proof that their scopes do not overlap. Repeated maintenance-year assessments are annual parcel stocks, not new investment flows. Mixed-use parcel assessments and taxable values are retained at whole-parcel scope and are not allocated to a data-center tenant or function by floor area. Operator-reported jobs supported remain distinct from direct employees and FTEs. Approved infrastructure grants are documented public commitments rather than verified disbursements or total public costs. Cumulative community funding remains separate from tax receipts, payroll and modeled multiplier effects. Reported facility power capacity is not measured electricity consumption or peak demand. Permit-listed emergency generators are not runtime, fuel-use or actual-emissions observations. A city largest-taxpayer table's personal-property assessment remains separate from the leasehold real-property account, tax bills, receipts and capital expenditure. TIF loan principal is financing rather than a grant or general-fund receipt; project-generated tax revenue pledged to repayment is retained as a separate public-financing flow and is not added to gross parcel distributions. Water-withdrawal and consumptive permit capacities are regulatory limits rather than measured use. Development-agreement local-labor preferences are requirements rather than realized participation, and operating employee snapshots remain distinct from customers' on-site staff and jobs forecasts. Audited City bond statements distinguish issuance draws, year-end principal, annual principal retired, interest and fees, pledged TIF revenue, debt-service-fund transfers and future principal-plus-interest commitments. These measures are not summed into a benefit or subsidy total. City pledged revenue, City debt-service-fund transfers and the private fund's project TIF revenue applied to loan repayment retain their separate source definitions because only the 2022 transfer and private-fund amount agree exactly. Developer testimony in public meeting minutes is retained as a source-attributed cumulative lower bound; local-contractor spending is not converted into payroll, worker counts, household spending or multiplier effects. Economic-improvement-district cost estimates and maximum owner assessments remain source projections until bond issuance, an assessment schedule, collections and expenditures are verified. A statutory financing cap is not a tax receipt, public expenditure or subsidy. Audited private equipment-financing balances are debt stocks rather than construction spending, public support or community benefit. Reported floor area and occupied-share values describe operating scale and utilization, not employment, revenue, power use or economic output. Contractor and engineer case studies document supplier roles and completion timing but do not establish payment amounts, worker residence, payroll or multiplier effects. State incentive contract amounts, expected jobs and paid-or-certified-to-date fields remain distinct; a zero paid/certified balance at an earlier reporting cutoff does not imply no later claims. Public charging-infrastructure awards are commitments rather than verified disbursements, private project investment or operating benefits. Qualitative payment descriptions without a defensible numeric bound remain research context rather than quantitative records. Program-reported actual qualified investment, certified tax-exemption value and certified tax-credit value remain separate cumulative measures; none is converted into annual spending, a cash grant, local revenue or causal impact. County Business Patterns observations are county-industry context, not project contributions: establishment counts are employer locations rather than data-center facilities, March employment is not an annual average, annual payroll spans the full NAICS cell, and disclosure noise, classification changes and geographic assignment limit comparisons. No CBP change is attributed to a study project. Project fragments: prj_study_im3_building_00364289074: Corrective public-source audit for Microsoft's data-center property at 5150 Rogers Road and explicitly labeled wider Microsoft/Bexar County activity. Exact-site ordinance, permit, appraisal, and tax-account records remain separate from later campuses and regional disclosures; the three appraisal accounts and two taxable-account payments are not consolidated. Permit value is administrative, the original investment and employment figures are commitments, the 2013 employment threshold is a reported lower bound, and the water quantity is a projection rather than metered consumption. No Bexar-and-Medina total is allocated to this property. Annual construction expenditure, construction labor and residence, supplier payments, operating payroll and purchases, recipient-level tax distributions, marginal public-service cost, electricity consumption, water withdrawal or consumption, wastewater, actual emissions, and a recurring facility-level community series remain unobserved after the documented searches. prj_study_im3_building_00377585075: Corrective DET01 evidence audit. Official parcel, permit, tax, water-account, state-certificate, EPA and operator records are retained as direct observations or clearly labeled source forecasts. Conflicting floor-area figures remain separate because their reporting definitions differ. Construction cost, realized jobs, supplier payments, community funding, electricity, emissions, wastewater, actual public-service cost and causal county effects remain unbounded rather than being filled with transferred assumptions. prj_study_im3_building_00460089167: Corrective primary-source audit adds current Andale parcel assessment, contractor-reported campus floor area, and two recipient- or government-reported Meta community grants. The search trail records useful and negative results across identity, tax, construction, jobs, suppliers, utilities, water, permits, public costs, incentives, community funding, and county comparison inputs. Campus-wide facts remain unallocated to the selected inventory building, overlapping community amounts are not added together, and unavailable supplier, payroll, utility-billing, discharge, generator, and marginal-service-cost amounts remain explicit gaps. prj_study_im3_building_00464097467: Second-pass public-evidence audit for Apple's Washoe County data-center campus at 21505 Reno Technology Parkway West and its 2024 expansion application. GOED audit findings, application forecasts, county permit values, parcel assessments, a water-right allocation, operator-reported electricity use, and recipient-reported donation bands remain separate evidence states and scopes. Permit values are administrative amounts and are not summed because overlapping scopes cannot be ruled out. Assessment values are parcel stocks, not investment or tax receipts. The 125 acre-foot water right is regulatory capacity, not measured use. Food Bank gifts are company-region transfers, not campus-attributable annual spending. No campus total is allocated to the selected mapped building; the four-building campus, later buildout cases, downtown Reno warehouse, supporting renewable projects, fire-station parcel, and more-than-200-person support statement are not collapsed into one footprint. No Switch Citadel or Storey County amount enters this fragment. Vendor payments, worker residence, taxes received by jurisdiction, realized 2024 abatement, same-scope public-service cost, wastewater, and building-level electricity or water remain unobserved. prj_study_im3_building_00664938835: Second-pass public-evidence audit for Expedient's adaptive reuse of the pre-existing data-center building at 4777 W Ironwood Drive. The review searched Franklin planning, agenda, assessment, permit, water and sewer materials; Milwaukee County tax and deed-record access points; Wisconsin DOR, WEDC, DFI and PSC records; operator press, specification, career, ESG and community pages; lease, financing, carrier and vendor disclosures; and archived official pages for 2007-2026. Opening-day and current operator specifications remain separate dated snapshots because the reported area and capacity changed. The county portal now establishes a 2021-2025 parcel-tax principal series, but not Expedient's incidence under the lease. The 2022 ownership transfer, assessments, estimated permit values, tax payments and hiring plan remain non-additive. No source was found for actual construction outlays, realized site employment or payroll, local procurement, Milwaukee-area community transfers, metered resources, project-attributable public costs or a fiscal net. prj_study_im3_building_01073720208: Second-pass public-evidence audit for Google's Council Bluffs data-center activity, retaining the selected inventory building as the project key while leaving campus, taxpayer-account, company-county, and state-award facts at their reported scopes. modeled_scope_note: Modeled contribution accounts for Apple Mesa / Maricopa County, Switch Citadel / Storey County, and Digital Crossroad Hammond / Lake County. Every required account category and county-comparison module contains sourced evidence or a visibly labeled modeled value. Public support is not netted against unmatched local revenues, unavailable public-service cost is represented by a break-even threshold rather than an invented net margin, county comparisons are descriptive rather than causal, and low-confidence transferred benchmarks remain explicit. Project fragments: prj_study_im3_building_00364289074: Corrective residual modeled account for Microsoft San Antonio. Eight transferred construction, labor, procurement, operating, and household-output scenarios were removed because their arbitrary capital shares, forecast-realization cases, local-purchase assumptions, and Virginia coefficients were not bounded by project observations. Only three low-confidence descriptive county comparisons remain: each uses the project's documented operating-by 2013 anchor and official Bexar County outcome data, has a finite fit-sensitivity envelope, and explicitly makes no causal attribution. The account intentionally remains incomplete because no defensible direct observation or residual model closes the supplier category. prj_study_im3_building_00377585075: Corrective DET01 synthesis. Only exact same-period tax-account arithmetic, its explicitly conditional public-cost break-even identity and a unit conversion of displayed municipal meter history remain. Construction, employment, supplier, household, electricity, cooling, emissions, wastewater and county-effect models were removed because the audit did not bound the missing project inputs. This account is intentionally incomplete where direct evidence remains unbounded. prj_study_im3_building_00460089167: Corrective audit retains six bounded residual calculations only: FY2025 county tax retained after the provisionally linked incentive, the identical marginal-service-cost break-even threshold, conversion of Meta-reported 2024 water withdrawal with source rounding, and three noncausal county comparison gaps with fit sensitivity. Ten models based on arbitrary capital timing, cost shares, FTE ratios, transferred operating/construction multipliers, fleet PUE, or wastewater ratios are removed. Supplier/local-procurement evidence remains unavailable, so the project is intentionally incomplete rather than backfilled. prj_study_im3_building_00464097467: Second-pass modeled contribution account after an expanded public-evidence audit. Direct county permits now cover historical construction values, assessor rolls cover a main-campus parcel stock, a county action covers water-right capacity, Apple reports 2025 campus electricity use, and recipient reports bound two community gifts. Those observations supersede the need for a modeled community proxy but do not supply Apple contractor job-years, construction payroll, annual operating payroll, supplier payments, taxes received, or public-service cost. The construction base therefore retains only the packet's explicit $163 million construction forecast and excludes equipment and historical capital; wide 0.5-1.5 transfer sensitivities expose the mismatch in the last-resort direct construction coefficients. The unsupported local-purchase-share and Virginia induced-output models are removed. No net-fiscal value or public-service-cost break-even is published. County outcome gaps remain descriptive benchmark applications with fit-sensitivity intervals and no causal-design metadata. prj_study_im3_building_00664938835: Second-pass Expedient Milwaukee / Franklin syntheses retained only after a documented 2007-2026 public-source audit. The account keeps a clearly labeled 2022 ownership-transfer anchor, a PB25-0303-only construction allocation sensitivity, an exact tax-equal public-cost break-even threshold, a capacity-based electricity engineering sensitivity, and three descriptive county comparison gaps. It removes transferred construction job-years, assumed local-purchase shares, supplier and household output extrapolations, and a duplicate modeled tax row because public sources did not establish realized site employment, supplier geography, household capture, or a need to restate the direct tax observations. PM25-0174 remains excluded for possible overlap. No synthesis is an observed result or fiscal net. prj_study_im3_building_01073720208: Second-pass governed synthesis for Google Council Bluffs. Construction job-years use only two directly observed September 2025 city permit valuations and transfer the published Prince William County prototype coefficients as benchmark equivalents; the four channels are separated and protected by one aggregation. No Pottawattamie County supplier-retention share is imposed because the public audit found contractor names but no payment or vendor-residence ledger. The water row is the unallocated Google Council Bluffs location identity reported for 2024, not a building allocation. No local abatement, exemption realization, franchise-fee amount, electric load, public-service cost, break-even threshold, or net fiscal result is modeled. County outcome gaps remain descriptive benchmark applications with fit-sensitivity ranges and no causal attribution.
legacy_first_entry_note: Nevada GOED identifies Apple's Washoe County campus and documents its December 2012 opening; the mapped footprint lies within that data-center complex. The evidence does not establish which of the campus buildings entered service first, a complete county inventory, or the absence of earlier government, university, telecom, utility, financial, healthcare, casino, or enterprise operations.

project_description: Apple's Washoe County data-center campus is located at 21505 Reno Technology Parkway West near Reno, Nevada, and is operated by Apple. The project key represents one mapped building, while source records describe a four-building campus that began operating in 2012, later buildout permits, supporting renewable projects, and a distinct 2024 expansion application; those boundaries are kept separate from tenant equipment and other Apple properties. County and operator records document completed construction activity, parcel development, water-right capacity, and campus-level electricity use.
